title: Daf (frame drum with rings)
summary: The daf is a large frame drum of Iran, a wide wooden frame with a goat-skin head and rows of loose metal rings fastened inside. Held upright in both hands and played with the fingers and palms, it gives a deep boom at the centre, a sharp tak at the edge and a shimmer of rings.
howToPlay: The head is lit in three places: the centre for Dum, a middle ring for Mid and an outer ring for Tak. The frame gives a Rim click and the rings a shimmer.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Let the rings shiver after each stroke; the Rings lane shakes them on their own.
Learn the slow cycle first, then the quick one.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The slow cycle counts six beats to the bar; the quick one counts four.
heritageNote: The daf is a frame drum of Iran and its neighbours, played in groups and in solo patterns that build slowly in speed. Makers set a band of loose rings inside the frame so that every stroke is followed by a shimmer.
